title: Persons or Science? A Philosophical Question
coreMove: Use scientific method without letting the method become the definition of the person.
sourcePressure: Rogers frames the relation between persons and science as a philosophical tension: science has power, but persons cannot be reduced to method alone. Frozen sidecar ch10 supports the heading, part placement, and broad thematic claims; it exposes no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the chapter into anti-science polemic or vague human mystery.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.

hook: opening with a definition of persons
counterintuition: Most people think X, but Y
It is not about being nice
The paradox is that acceptance changes everything
